transcript.text: This is one food item that I would never ever touch as a nutritionist.
Can you guess what it is?
The moment I said that, something must have come to all your minds. [Original HI: But mere aise bolte hi aap sab ke dimaag mein kuch aaya hoga.]
Someone must have thought sugar, someone Maggi, someone maida, [Original HI: Kisi ne socha hoga cheeni, kisi ne Maggi, kisi ne maida,]
and someone rice. The reason is fear-mongering. [Original HI: aur kisi ne chawal. Iska reason hai fear mongering.]
Every other day you're being scared of some food item. [Original HI: Aaye din aapko har food item se daraya ja raha hai.]
'Don't eat this, don't eat that.' [Original HI: Yeh mat khao, woh mat khao.]
But nobody tells you the truth, that no single food is healthy or unhealthy. [Original HI: Lekin koi aapko yeh sachchai nahi batata ki koi ek cheez healthy ya unhealthy nahi hoti.]
It's your overall diet.
For example, you eat protein-rich food and fibre-rich fruits and veggies all day, [Original HI: Example, aap din bhar protein rich food, fibre rich fruits and veggies khate ho,]
then add a spoon of sugar to your chai, [Original HI: phir chai mein ek chammach cheeni daal lete ho,]
so has your diet become unhealthy? [Original HI: toh kya yeh diet unhealthy hogyi?]
But if you eat a salad in the morning, [Original HI: Lekin wahi agar aap subah mein salad khate ho,]
but then all day only desserts, deep-fried food, packaged food, [Original HI: but phir din bhar sirf desserts, deep fried food, packaged food,]
with no protein or fibre,
is that diet healthy? [Original HI: toh kya yeh diet healthy hui kya?]
Stop demonizing food.
Divide food into only two kinds: [Original HI: Khane ko sirf 2 tarike mein baanto:]
food that is nutritionally dense,
or food with low nutritional value,
and make room for both in your diet. [Original HI: aur apni diet mein dono ke liye jagah banao.] [partly unclear]
[Film clip, partly unclear] [Original HI: Woh, Shakti, jo usko villain...]
So from today, being scared of food items is banned. Keep a healthy lifestyle [Original HI: Toh aaj se food items se darna mana hai, healthy lifestyle rakho]
and stay away from people who say... [Original HI: aur door raho aise logo se jo bole ki...]

hook.text: This is one food item that I would never ever touch as a nutritionist. Can you guess what it is?
hook.template: This is one [THING] I would never [ACTION] as a [EXPERT]. Can you guess what it is?
hook.whyItWorks: A covered steel cloche plus 'never ever touch as a nutritionist' makes everyone guess, and guessing is engagement. The twist is that the cloche is never opened: the 'banned food' was a trap to make the point about fear-mongering, which rewards viewers who stayed for the reveal.

format.visualLayout: Seated talking head behind a covered cloche, orange caption boxes, thought-bubble graphics, illustrated title cards, stock b-roll and a Bollywood clip
format.pacing: fast, about 1 cut every 1.5 to 2s with graphics popping in on almost every line
format.reasoning: The unopened cloche holds attention for the whole minute, and the quick graphics (sugar sack, Maggi, maida, rice) mirror what the viewer is guessing. Stock b-roll for the 'chai with a spoon of sugar' vs 'salad then junk all day' examples makes the comparison concrete.

angle.topic: Food fear and labelling foods healthy or unhealthy
angle.angle: No single food is healthy or unhealthy; your overall diet is
angle.commonBelief: Some foods like sugar, maida, Maggi or rice are bad and must be cut
angle.contrarianTake: A spoon of sugar in an otherwise good diet doesn't ruin it; judge foods as nutrient-dense or low-value and make room for both

myVersion.hook: Rice, ghee, aloo, chai. Which one did someone tell you to quit first?
myVersion.script:
Rice, ghee, aloo, chai. Which one did someone tell you to quit first?
Mine was rice. I was told rice makes you fat, so for a whole year I didn't touch it.
Guess what? I didn't lose a single extra kilo because of that.
Here's what nobody tells you.
Your body doesn't judge one food. It responds to the whole day on your plate.
Let me show you two days.
Day one. Poha with peanuts in the morning. Dal, rice, sabzi and curd for lunch. A fruit in the evening. Roti, paneer and salad at night. And yes, one chai with a teaspoon of sugar.
Is that an unhealthy day because of one teaspoon? Of course not.
Day two. Just a green smoothie for breakfast because you're 'being good.'
Then you're starving, so it's biscuits at work, a packet of namkeen at four, and a pizza at night because you deserve it.
No rice. No sugar in chai. Still the worse day by far.
So stop asking 'is this food good or bad?'
Ask, 'what is this food giving me?'
Protein, fibre, vitamins, real fullness? Eat it often.
Mostly just taste? Keep it, enjoy it, have it less.
That's it. No banned list. No fear.
And if someone tells you one food is ruining your health, ask them what else you're eating.
Comment the food you were told to quit, and I'll tell you how to fit it back in.
